candidates.demonstrated_gap: Targets open gap 2 (native Workflow hard crash, physical-host reboot and remote cancellation are unqualified) and edit ownership. Neither winner keeps durable, harness-independent ownership state. Claude Code agent teams are 'experimental and disabled by default', and '/resume and /rewind do not restore in-process teammates'. LoopX is 'a deterministic (no-LLM) control plane' that sits on the native hosts rather than replacing them. It ships a durable state kernel: goals, typed todos, peer claims and leases, user gates, validated writeback, quota-aware scheduling and cross-turn continuation. Its README says this state stays durable 'across days, restarts, and harnesses' and that LoopX never turns 'an unverified run into evidence of success'. Host paths: Codex CLI `$loopx` drives a visible `/goal`. Claude Code runs `/loopx` plus native `/loop`, gated by the LoopX MCP tools should_run, claim_task and complete_task; this adapter is opt-in and never installed by default, and its own README does not mark it experimental. It installs with `python3 -m pip install --upgrade loopx` and uses the hosts' existing sign-ins, so no new credentials are needed. The only measured data is upstream's own LHTB study: 46 tasks on GPT-5.6 Sol, one trial per task, unequal budgets. LoopX 1.0.3 Heartbeat scored 0.4948 mean reward, against 0.4475 for native Codex Goal and 0.4218 for Plain Codex; strict solves were 7/46, 4/46 and 7/46. This must be re-measured on the stack's current GPT-6.1 Sol. Limits: the product is Codex-first, so the trial should start there. The Claude adapter's --harden gate is 'not a sandbox'. Cross-host shared goals are only a stated direction. Five advisories were published on 2026-08-12, including GHSA-c42j-vw98-9jqm (high): OS command injection through worker_turn_command in the multi-agent launcher, which is this layer's own surface. It affects versions before 0.4.5 and is patched in 0.4.5; the patched versions of the other four were not verified. Never deploy it as a root systemd service.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run the layer's frozen representative task under Harbor or Inspect (never a self-written runner), with equal budgets and at least 3 repetitions, in three arms. Arm A: native single agent. Arm B: the native worker graph (Claude Code 2.1.290 or later with Workflow and subagents using worktree isolation, and Codex subagents). Arm C: the same host under LoopX, Codex CLI `$loopx` first, then Claude Code `/loopx` plus `/loop`. Inject kill -9 of the host mid-turn plus a WSL restart, a peer edit collision on one file, a cancellation, and a user gate that must block. Metrics: turns resumed versus restarted from their prompt; lost or duplicated edits and effects; claim or lease violations; gate bypasses (must be 0); independent acceptance rate; and complete usage (token delta between provider-reported and persisted usage). LoopX is adopted for long-running research workers only if it recovers with zero lost or duplicated edits and zero gate bypasses where native loses state, at equal or better acceptance and usage. It is refuted if native 2.1.290 or later recovers equally.

candidates.demonstrated_gap:
Symphony is OpenAI's own orchestrator for the surviving alternative, Codex native workers. It runs only through the Codex app-server and has no Claude Code runner. On paper it adds what the winners lack:
- a tracker-backed work queue;
- cancellation by tracker state: a terminal state stops the agent and cleans the workspace, while a non-active state stops it without cleanup (SPEC 14.4);
- per-issue workspace containment, plus a Codex workspace-write sandbox rooted at the issue workspace (Elixir safer defaults);
- optional SSH multi-host workers (SPEC Appendix A);
- absolute thread-total token accounting (SPEC 13.5).

It does NOT close the crash/reboot gap. Scheduler state is in memory by design. After a restart, retry timers, running sessions and blocked approval waits are not restored (SPEC 14.3). The Elixir README says blocked entries are cleared on restart and become dispatchable again. So the 'durable approval waits' condition in overturn_when fails.

The review gate is procedural, not enforced. The agent holds tracker-write tools. The land skill squash-merges with gh pr merge from inside the workspace once checks are green and Codex Review comments are acknowledged. The human gate is a Linear state: the issue sits in Human Review until a human moves it to Merging.

Credentials reach further than the tracker token. Symphony strips only declared tracker-token variables from the Codex child. The push and merge steps therefore use whatever gh credentials the child's HOME exposes; on this host that is the operator's own login, which covers more than one repository. Whether the workspace-write sandbox blocks reading that config is not established here.

The walkthrough-video part of proof of work depends on the launch-app and github-pr-media skills. WORKFLOW.md names them, but the repo does not ship them: .codex/skills at be10a1b79df7 holds only commit, debug, land, linear, pull, push and release.

Linear is not required. The Elixir reference also ships GitHub Issues, Jira Cloud, Asana and GitLab adapters. But the GitHub adapter accepts only open/closed states (github/adapter.ex). A trial without a new account must therefore enforce review through GitHub branch protection (a required approving review plus required checks) and tracker.required_labels, not tracker states.

The trusted-environment warning rules out the shipped elixir/WORKFLOW.md settings (approval_policy: never, networkAccess: true, shell_environment_policy.inherit=all) on any repository where untrusted people can write issue text. Codex's ignore_default_excludes defaults to true, so inherit=all passes every non-tracker KEY/SECRET/TOKEN environment variable to agent shell commands. fp-check rates this a true positive for the shipped configuration, not an upstream bug, since upstream limits Symphony to trusted environments.

The Elixir build is 'prototype software intended for evaluation only', and upstream recommends a self-hardened build from SPEC.md. That build is a separate coordinator decision; this label covers a bounded evaluation only.

Maintenance: created 2026-02-26, so not too new to assess. 24 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08; latest be10a1b79df7 on 2026-09-15.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Setup for a bounded evaluation on linux-wsl2:
- Elixir/Erlang via mise, the installed Codex 0.160.x app-server, and a private scratch repository using the GitHub Issues adapter.
- A dedicated OS user, or a dedicated HOME/GH_CONFIG_DIR, whose only GitHub credential is a fine-grained token limited to the scratch repository.
- codex.command sets shell_environment_policy.inherit=core (or none) and shell_environment_policy.ignore_default_excludes=false explicitly, because the config reference read does not state the inherit default.
- Symphony's safer defaults for omitted fields (reject-object approval_policy, workspace-write), required_labels set, and branch protection on main requiring one approving review and the required checks.

The same frozen task and failure contract also runs on native Claude Code workers (isolation: worktree) and native Codex workers. Cases:
1. Cancellation: close the issue mid-run, and separately remove the required label. The agent stops, and the non-terminal path keeps the workspace.
2. Replay: kill the orchestrator mid-turn and restart it. Record what is re-dispatched and whether partial edits and failed attempts survive.
3. Ownership: no writes outside the per-issue workspace.
4. Integration: no merge before the required review.
5. Usage: Symphony's thread totals compared with the native counters.

Verdict rule:
- Symphony is refuted if land merges before approval, if a restart loses work the native path keeps, or if any step needs a credential beyond that fine-grained token. Check the last point by listing the credentials visible inside the workspace shell.
- It earns adoption only if it passes every frozen case and adds one the native path fails, such as tracker-driven re-dispatch after an orchestrator kill or dispatch to an SSH host.

candidates.demonstrated_gap:
Xum is a different kind of tool from the desktop cockpits. It was renamed from coder/mux: GitHub resolves the old name to coder/xum, but the README's install link and the mux.coder.com docs still use the old name.

Xum runs its own agent loop ('Xum has a custom agent loop') instead of driving the native CLIs. It offers Local, Worktree and SSH runtimes and a central view of git divergence. With its SSH runtime, it is the only tool reviewed here that dispatches workers to a remote host natively.

Credentials: no new third-party account is strictly needed.
- The built-in OpenAI provider supports Codex OAuth.
- Custom providers (openai-compatible, openai-responses or anthropic-messages, with a baseUrl and an optional apiKeyFile) can point at the OmniRoute gateway.
- Claude models need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or a gateway; no Claude subscription login is documented.

Because Xum replaces the winner's agent loop, its quality on this requirement is unmeasured. It has to be judged as an agent harness, which puts it close to the native-clients layer, rather than as a worker manager.

candidates.demonstrated_gap:
RD-Agent is a north-star research worker, not a replacement for this layer. RD-Agent(Q) automates the factor and model R&D loop:
- a Research stage forms hypotheses;
- the Co-STEER Development stage generates code;
- Qlib backtests feed results back;
- a bandit scheduler chooses the next direction.
No foundation worker graph provides that loop.

It fails this layer's 'integrate only after relevant review' rule. The feedback stage accepts results by backtest metrics alone, with no external review gate. The trading catalog's qlib entry already records multiple-testing bias and model cost for automated factor mining.

Fit facts:
- Linux only.
- Most scenarios need Docker usable without sudo.
- conda with Python 3.10 or 3.11.
- A LiteLLM backend that needs ChatCompletion, json_mode and embeddings. Chat can use an OpenAI-compatible base URL. Whether the OmniRoute gateway serves embeddings is unverified; the documented alternative is a litellm_proxy embedding endpoint, which can be local.
- v1.0.0 breaking change: UI_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN is now required even on localhost, and General Model uploads accept actual files only. The token is self-generated, not a third-party credential.

Market fit:
- The shipped Qlib templates default to cn_data, csi300 and SH000300.
- The paper's main results are on CSI 300. It extends out-of-sample to CSI 500 and NASDAQ 100 (train 2008-2021, test 2024-01 to 2025-06) and takes fundamentals from the Wind terminal.
- No point-in-time US-equities qualification exists, and this report does not assert US fit.

A bounded run is a separate qualification unit in research-factors-ml, where Qlib is listed as unqualified.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: It offers one orchestration and policy layer over both clients this stack runs, through the official `claude` and `codex` CLIs and existing subscriptions (install with `uv tool install omnigent`). Its Polly example plans, delegates coding sub-agents (Claude Code, Codex or Pi) into parallel git worktrees, and routes each diff to a reviewer from a different vendor before a human merges. Policies can pause for approval before risky actions, cap spend, or limit tools per server, agent or chat. On Linux, agent terminals run in a mandatory bwrap sandbox. That matches overturn_when's approval waits and open gap 4 (restricted role). But Claude Code natively has per-agent tool limits and permission modes, and Codex natively has per-agent `sandbox_mode = "read-only"`. The gap is therefore cross-harness uniformity, not a missing capability. Against it: alpha status, and its README has no benchmark or eval. Seven advisories were published against exactly this policy and containment layer. They include critical GHSA-598r-29w2-g93q (2026-09-16: a per-terminal os_env.cwd bypasses the workspace guard) and high GHSA-7mqg-cx4g-x2rf (2026-06-29: the guardrail shell-command parser fails open).
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run this once a real task needs approval waits or restricted roles across both Claude Code and Codex workers. On the frozen task under Harbor or Inspect, plant a policy-violating command and a review-blocking defect, run one restricted Bash-only worker, and kill one worker mid-run. Compare native controls (Claude Code permissions, hooks and sandbox; Codex per-agent sandbox_mode) against Omnigent policies with cross-vendor review. Metrics: policy bypasses and out-of-scope writes (must be 0); approval waits honored and resumed; lost edits; seeded-defect catch rate; and complete usage.
evidence: https://github.com/omnigent-ai/omnigent: README. A meta-harness over Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Hermes and Pi. Subscriptions work through the official claude and codex CLIs. Status badge: alpha. No benchmark terms in the README.

Upstream GHSA-pxhw-h44j-8pfx is CVE-2026-87766 (high, CVSS 8.8, CWE-22/CWE-59; versions below 0.12.0 are vulnerable, patched in 0.12.0). Per the advisory, 'When bubblewrap creates a file in /newroot it may follow a symlink in a parent that points to /oldroot', which creates files on the host as the launching uid. srt makes bubblewrap create files on content the sandbox can write. PR #618 says 'an absent denyWrite path is blocked by an empty file (mount point) that bubblewrap makes on the host', and README L745 says 'it first creates a mount point there: an empty, read-only file (or an empty directory...)'. That matches the advisory's precondition. fp-check verdict: TRUE that the host bwrap lacks the fix (package changelog plus advisory range). candidates.demonstrated_gap: The installed native client codex-cli 0.160.1 ships `codex sandbox [COMMAND]...`. Its README says 'The CLI surface is `codex sandbox`; the host OS selects the sandbox backend' (linux-sandbox README L111). The layer has never compared it with the winner. On paper at rust-v0.160.1 it handles three open sandbox-runtime (srt) gaps differently. (a) Readiness, gap 2: the managed-proxy bridge waits for an explicit readiness byte (HOST_BRIDGE_READY, proxy_routing.rs L48, L169-175, L345-349, L362-367; error text 'host bridge did not acknowledge readiness'). The README says seccomp blocks new AF_UNIX/socketpair creation 'after the bridge is live' (L85-89). srt 0.0.77 and 0.0.78 start their socat relays in the background, and the fix exists only on srt main (PR #639). (b) Overlapping path rules, gap 3: split-policy entries are applied in path-specificity order, so narrower denied subpaths win (L53-58), and symlink-in-path or missing protected paths are masked with /dev/null (L78-80). srt instead documents a read-denied directory as an 'EMPTY WRITABLE directory' tmpfs that discards writes (srt README v0.0.78 L440). (c) Network, gap 0: weaker on paper. The codex network-proxy README blocks hostnames that resolve to local or private IPs by 'best-effort DNS lookup' and says 'DNS rebinding is hard to fully prevent without pinning the resolved IP(s)' (L249-251, L264-267). srt dials the address that passed its check, with 'no second lookup' (srt README L361). Codex limited mode allows only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS and needs MITM for HTTPS (L253-255). The in-sandbox bridge listener binds IPv4 127.0.0.1 only (proxy_routing.rs L391-404); IPv6 behaviour is untested. Defaults: `codex sandbox` applies the active config's effective permission profile (debug_sandbox.rs L273) and starts the managed proxy only when the profile configures network (L353-373). Restricted network without the proxy uses --unshare-net (README L83-84). Limits shared with srt: Codex prefers the first `bwrap` on PATH outside the cwd (README L10-16). On this host that is the same /usr/bin/bwrap 0.11.1-1ubuntu0.3 that lacks the CVE-2026-87766 fix. The vendored fallback runs only when no bwrap is on PATH; it is bubblewrap 0.11.2 per NEWS.md, and its bubblewrap.c has no openat2/RESOLVE_IN_ROOT (other files were not checked). Resource limits were not found in linux-sandbox/README.md at the tag, so gap 4 is unchanged. On macOS it uses Seatbelt profiles (codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt*.sbpl), the same OS primitive as srt.

candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20261006-runtimes: Found in this sweep's GraphQL triage of agent microVM sandboxes, then verified through its README, docs site and the GitHub API.
candidates.demonstrated_gap:
Gondolin documents the strongest egress confinement for the cases srt's gap-0 receipt still lists as untested: IPv6 deny, direct queries to a public resolver, DNS rebinding (cause undetermined) and TLS termination. Per the security design's Egress Capability Matrix:
- guest traffic ends in a host-side policy stack where only HTTP and TLS pass by default, checked against hostname allowlists plus DNS and IP checks
- HTTP CONNECT is denied and unknown protocols are dropped
- UDP is blocked except port 53
- DNS defaults to 'synthetic', with no upstream lookups, so DNS cannot be used as an egress channel

Secrets are injected host-side, and only for allowed destinations (README L45-46). VM-level sandbox.cpus and sandbox.memory exist on both backends (backends page).

It is not targeted because its own docs exclude what gap 4 needs. The non-goals include 'VM escape / hypervisor bugs ... a QEMU escape is a host compromise' and 'Denial of service ... no complete DoS isolation'. No host-side jail around QEMU is documented, whereas BoxLite documents one.

Its fit on WSL2 x86_64 is weaker than on the Macs. README L114 says 'ARM64 is the most tested runtime path today', and L79 lists qemu-system-arm as the Linux prerequisite. QEMU guests can match qemu-system-x86_64, though, and a linux-x64 krun runner package exists. There is no QUIC or generic UDP (limitations page). It has 0 published advisories, which means none among what was assessed, not a clean verdict.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run the battery's network and cleanup halves on v0.13.0, against BoxLite's allow_net and srt. Cover IPv4 and IPv6 deny, direct IP, UDP 53 to a public resolver, rebinding names that resolve to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, TLS SNI/Host mismatch, and CONNECT or SOCKS. Run them on a Mac (arm64) and on WSL2 with an x86_64 guest under KVM acceleration. Add in-VM memory and fork caps with host-side QEMU limits.

Gondolin becomes the targeted candidate if it is the only candidate with zero forbidden egress and its caps hold. It is dropped if x86_64 guests are not KVM-accelerated on WSL2, or if the simulation fixture needs non-HTTP egress.

candidates.demonstrated_gap:

- No seccomp, jailer or sandbox-exec layer around the VMM is documented anywhere in the 488-line README.

candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20261006-runtimes: Found in this sweep's GraphQL triage of maintained agent sandboxes, which queried always-further/nono and was redirected to nolabs-ai/nono. A web search located the nono docs, and docs.rs, the README and GitHub API advisories were read.
candidates.demonstrated_gap:
A same-class head-to-head with the actual winner, srt: OS primitives, no VM, both hosts. Two srt defects reproduced on Linux are tied to its mechanism:
- Readiness race. The gap-wave2 receipt 2-readiness-race-quantified.json recorded 8/8 first requests failing (curl exit 7) on srt 0.0.77. Its in-sandbox socat relays remained after upstream PR #257, and no upstream fix was found.
- Silent overlapping-deny write. Receipt 3-overlapping-denyread-write-reproduced.json recorded write_exit=0, the host unchanged, and an ephemeral overlay hiding the directory.

nono 0.79.0 describes itself as a 'Capability-based sandboxing library using Landlock (Linux) and Seatbelt (macOS)' (docs.rs). On Linux it therefore enforces kernel access rights rather than bubblewrap bind or overlay mounts, so neither defect's mechanism exists in its design. This is unmeasured. It is not established that nono can express the same overlapping deny-read and allow-write policy, because Landlock grants are additive. nono's own proxy start-up ordering is also untested. Egress goes through profiles carrying a network allowlist, a credential proxy and L7 filtering (README L109, L133-134, L189).

The trial is feasible now, with no host change. This WSL2 kernel has CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK=y with landlock first in CONFIG_LSM, and landlock_create_ruleset reports ABI 7 (TCP rules need ABI 4 or later). README L94 lists WSL2. The repository was renamed: always-further/nono now resolves to nolabs-ai/nono.

These risks are recorded but not decisive:
- nono is pre-1.0 (README L33).
- It has 12 published advisories. They include network-policy bypasses fixed in 0.74.0 (GHSA-6hww, GHSA-7q3j, GHSA-gcpc, the last a DNS tunnel via the proxy) and a high seccomp x86_64 legacy-ABI bypass (GHSA-vhq2, fixed in 0.74.0).
- Two high records still show no patched release. They are GHSA-8r33 (an L7 endpoint path-policy bypass in nono-proxy, '>=0.73.0: Not yet') and GHSA-wjv5 (a tool-sandbox shim fall-through, 'not yet released'). The v0.78.0 notes list both, so their status is unresolved. Both concern nono-only features that an srt-parity trial would leave disabled.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run nono v0.79.0, with L7 endpoint rules and tool-sandbox shims disabled, and a version-recorded srt on the gap-wave2 fixtures. On WSL2 this needs no host change. Repeat on both Macs, where both tools use Seatbelt, so the Mac half compares policy generation rather than mechanism. Measure:
- (a) First-request success over 100 cold starts without retries, against srt's 8/8 failures in receipt 2.
- (b) The receipt 3 overlapping deny-read and write fixture: either nono expresses it and the write exits non-zero, or record it as inexpressible.
- (c) The receipt 0 egress cases plus IPv6 deny, NAT64 and IPv4-mapped targets, UDP 53 to a public resolver, and TLS SNI/Host mismatch. Landlock ABI 7 has no UDP rules, so record what blocks UDP.
- (d) Cleanup.

nono replaces srt only with zero forbidden successes and no readiness failures. It is overturned by any forbidden success that srt blocks, by a stack policy it cannot express, or by GHSA-8r33 or GHSA-wjv5 staying unpatched for a feature the selected policy needs.

candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20261006-runtimes: Seeded by the completeness critic's follow-up (class 1: external heartbeat). Verified with gh api and the repository's own docs at master.
candidates.demonstrated_gap: The layer has no out-of-band detector for a missed or silent run, and two kinds of failure need one. (a) Host loss: when the WSL2 PC reboots, loses power, or its user manager crashes, Dagu and systemd stop with it. Dagu's catch-up (#1180; #2742 in v2.16.4; catchup_window inheritance fix #2770 in v2.16.6) acts only after the scheduler returns. On the Macs, Apple documents that a StartCalendarInterval job missed while the machine is powered off never runs. (b) Silent skips on a healthy host: dagucloud/dagu#2970 (closed 2026-10-03) reports a scheduled run silently skipped while any run of the DAG is queued. v2.18.2 only logs the skipped slot (#2980), so nothing alerts. Healthchecks is a dead man's switch (introduction.md L3-11). It offers Simple, Cron and OnCalendar schedules (configuring_checks.md L33; OnCalendar is systemd-timer syntax). Cron schedules take an expression, the server's time zone and a grace time (L52-67), so a weekday America/New_York market-hours job maps directly. Grace Time also bounds the gap from start to success (L39-50). /start marks a run that never finishes as down after grace and records durations (measuring_script_run_time.md L3-31, L50-53). It ships an ntfy integration (hc/integrations/ntfy). Self-hosting needs Python 3.12+ and Django 6.0, with SQLite as the default store (self_hosted.md L11-13, L57-58). Alerts are sent only while a separately supervised `sendalerts` process runs (L68-70, L148-150). Gatus heartbeats are fixed-interval and have no start/duration signal, so Healthchecks is the better semantic fit for calendar-scheduled data and research jobs and for detecting hangs.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: This is a bounded trial, and both the monitor and its alert path sit off the WSL2 host. The stack's ntfy is a loopback topic on the workstation (adoption/templates/systemd/host-requests-workstation.service L10), so a host failure would take notification down with it. The off-host alert route is part of the trial. Arms: Healthchecks, with its web process and sendalerts both supervised, against Gatus external-endpoint heartbeats as the comparison arm. Frozen cases: (1) WSL2 host powered off, or the systemd user manager killed, while a slot is due; measure time-to-alert against configured grace. (2) A slot skipped on a healthy host, reproducing the #2970 queued-run skip. (3) A /start with no finish (hang). (4) A nonzero exit. (5) A duplicate run. (6) A weekend or holiday gap for a weekday cron job; count false alerts. (7) Restart of the monitor host; check retained state and history. Metrics: detection latency, false alerts, history kept per check, off-host alert delivery, and the processes and memory needed to operate. Healthchecks is overturned if Gatus detects cases 1-4 with equal latency and no more false alerts at lower operating cost, or if Healthchecks misses case 2 or 3.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The layer records no native scheduling surface for agent-run (model) workloads, although claude-code is in its components_vs_upstream. The installed client (2.1.291) has three. (1) /loop and the cron tools are session-scoped. Recurring tasks expire after 7 days (official docs; a third-party search summary saying 3 days is wrong). They fire only while the REPL is idle, run up to 10% of the period late (max 15 min), and in this worker session the CronCreate schema says 'durable' has no effect. (2) Desktop scheduled tasks run on the local machine while the app is open. Their 'Review history' lists every past run, including skipped runs with the reason (asleep, previous run still in progress, other tasks running), and tasks can be paused, resumed and deleted. (3) Routines run in Anthropic's cloud. They are a research preview, start from a fresh clone with no local files, run at most hourly, and are subject to hourly caps and subscription usage. Their list_runs history omits fires skipped before a session existed (RemoteTrigger schema). Only routines survive loss of the WSL2 host, and they cannot reach local data or research state, so none of the three closes the host-failure gap for local workloads. Desktop's skipped-run history is something a Dagu-run `claude -p` job does not record natively. Reliability is still moving. 2.1.290 fixed extra runs on resume, respawn or fork; tasks that never fired after a /background hand-off; tasks lost after compaction; and wakeups silently lost when background sessions were restarted through updates and low memory (CHANGELOG L28-29, L133, L164). 2.1.274 fixed a routine firing twice after an edit (L1534). Score whether every skipped or duplicate run is recorded with its cause, cancellation latency, whether the local process tree and the remote model run (billing) stop, usage accounting, and lines of glue. A native surface replaces Dagu for agent jobs only if it records every skipped or duplicate run and stops runs cleanly with less glue. Otherwise Dagu keeps scheduling and the native surfaces stay conveniences.

candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20261006-runtimes: Web search for single-binary durable execution engines (an everydev.ai listing was the lead), confirmed through the GitHub releases, README, contributors and commits APIs.
candidates.demonstrated_gap: Obelisk is the only surveyed durable engine with Dagu's footprint that also runs native host processes. It ships as one binary with embedded SQLite and an embedded web UI, with prebuilt x86_64 Linux and aarch64 macOS archives. Exec activities (since v0.38.0) run host executables and collect stdout and stderr. In v0.42.0 (2026-10-04), an exec activity's process group is killed and reaped when its lock expires or the executor shuts down, which prevents overlap with a retry (#1022). The default execution lock expiry is now 30 s, and [limits] cells cap exec processes (default 32). A crashed executor's work therefore becomes retryable through lock expiry, without a separate scheduler process. That bound is documented only. Dagu's comparable figure (about 182 s, with a scheduler required) was measured at its default stale-run detection, and no matched-configuration run exists. Bounded-tree acceptance would still come from systemd cgroup containment, the same as on the Dagu path. Workflows are WASM components or JavaScript (workflow-js), so Python research jobs would run as exec activities. It stays at compare, not targeted, for maintenance and supply-chain reasons. The README says 'Pre-release: Expect changes in CLI, gRPC, WIT, and database schema'. Each of v0.40.0, v0.41.0 and v0.42.0 carries breaking configuration, API or schema changes: 0.42 splits server.toml, requires an app name, moves the SQLite directory and stops publishing to crates.io. The contributors API lists one human contributor (tomasol, 6406 contributions); the other entries are bots.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: No measured gap today. This proposal depends on the in-winner Next.js static-export test. The fixture runs two runtime processes: `next start` (Node, 127.0.0.1:18080, /api rewrite; package.json L12) and uvicorn 0.53.0 serving FastAPI (serve.py L33, 127.0.0.1:18081). The 2026-09-26 and 2026-09-29 refuters left one open question for this layer: Next.js server mode rests on incumbency. It is testable as output:'export' served from the FastAPI process. If that arm passes, a single ASGI process serves both the API and the static UI, and the server choice beneath the FastAPI winner becomes a live decision. Granian v2.8.4 serves a static tree from Rust, outside the Python event loop (--static-path-mount, --static-path-dir-to-file index.html, --static-path-expires), and offers RSS-capped worker recycling (--workers-max-rss). In the control arm, Starlette StaticFiles serves the export inside the app. Two capabilities were verified not to be differentiators: HTTP/2, which uvicorn 0.54.0 README L30 supports, and worker respawn, since uvicorn docs/deployment/index.md L77 says its process manager restarts dead children. Then run both arms on the WSL2 workstation and an M5 Pro Mac, with identical lockfiles and the same supervisor (systemd or launchd). Arm A: uvicorn 0.54.0 with Starlette StaticFiles serving out/. Arm B: Granian 2.8.4 `--interface asgi --static-path-mount out --static-path-dir-to-file index.html`. Both arms must pass the fixture's 12 pytest API/database tests and its Playwright checks. Measure cold start to first 200, idle and loaded RSS, p50/p99 latency for / and one /api route under the same upstream load generator at fixed concurrency, and kill -9 recovery time. candidates.demonstrated_gap: This is a model-level, newest-technique gap on the stack's own qualified route, and it needs no new component. The frozen WSL RTX 4090 route (native-agent-stack@ecfa1127 blueprints/convergence-practice/gpu-inference/plan.json) runs without speculative decoding. It uses b11057, Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M, partial offload at 32 GPU layers, temperature 0 with top_k 1, and a latency_rule that reports cold load, first content and generation separately. DSpark extends DFlash with a semi-autoregressive Markov head, so each draft forward pass emits a whole block. It is documented as '--spec-type draft-dspark' in docs/speculative.md, and that file is byte-identical at the stack's pin b11057 and at v0.6.0 (diffed). common/arg.cpp at b11057 already handles COMMON_SPECULATIVE_TYPE_DRAFT_DSPARK (L378-380). This corrects the critic's premise: DSpark needs no pin bump. Speculative decoding is 'exact under greedy decoding' (LFM2.5-VL-3B-DSpark card), which matches the route's greedy settings, so the 12-test oracle should be unaffected while generation time may fall; the size of the gain under partial offload is a hypothesis to measure. The drafter is the constraint. llama.cpp says 'Currently only drafts with a Qwen3 backbone are supported', and the Qwen3.8-27B DSpark drafters from the last two weeks are community speculators-format uploads (for example inference-optimization/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark-FP8-DYNAMIC, 2026-09-28). No Qwen-org drafter appears among the 60 newest DSpark repositories. v0.6.0 (2026-10-05) matters for a Mac arm: it adds few-row MMA Metal kernels for speculative and batched decoding (#29869) and probabilistic sampling for simple draft and MTP (#27694).

Otherwise run an A/B in the same host state, at least 3 runs each: the frozen plan unchanged vs the frozen plan plus '-md <drafter.gguf> --spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max <block>'. Pass if all of the following hold: the text matches the no-draft baseline at temperature 0; the oracle passes 12/12; generation time improves by a margin declared in advance; VRAM stays within the plan's admission budget; and the server recovers after a restart. Refute on low acceptance (no gain), divergent output, or a VRAM admission failure. This is the winner's own 0.160.1 surface compared with the stack's current integration; it is not a replacement. The worker (blueprints/us-equities/workers/native_worker.py at ecfa1127) runs one in-process stdio app-server per run through the vendor's openai_codex Python SDK. Gap-wave2 receipts at SDK/native 0.155.1 already settled new-process resume and a dynamic-tool round trip. The installed 0.160.1 may meet two overturn_when needs without a new SDK.
(1) Remote/container worker, which overturn_when currently assigns to the OpenHands SDK. `codex exec-server` is [EXPERIMENTAL]; its `forward` subcommand registers 'an existing WebSocket exec-server as a remote environment'. The protocol has experimental environment/add|info|status ('Adds or replaces a remote environment by id'). This would keep the native Codex loop and move tool execution off the host, which is the limit the gap-2 isolation receipt records.
(2) Multi-client session control. thread/resume, thread/fork, turn/steer and turn/interrupt are stable, and thread/queue/add|list|update|delete|reorder|start are experimental. They are served by `codex app-server --listen unix://|ws://` or by the shared daemon behind `codex agents` and `codex queue --thread`.

The trial uses only the local exec-server forward path, and that path's credential requirements are unverified. The OpenAI Agents API self-hosted path also runs exec-server, but it needs OPENAI_API_KEY with api.agents.* scopes, a separate environment key and @openai/codex@alpha. It is excluded as a paid API with new credentials on a prerelease.

Gap 1's provider-consumption clause stays open natively. turn/interrupt returns {}, and account/usage/read gives only account-level lifetime and daily-bucket ChatGPT token activity.

candidates.demonstrated_gap:
This anchors to the Claude arm of open_gaps[1] ('Claude Agent SDK interruption reports usage as unavailable').

At v0.86.0 the adapter is TypeScript and depends on @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.287 and @agentclientprotocol/sdk 1.7.0. It implements newSession, loadSession, resumeSession, listSessions, closeSession, cancel and unstable_forkSession. On session/cancel it settles the prompt with stopReason 'cancelled' and a usage object. It also force-settles a wedged query.next() after a grace period (issue #680).

The usage on cancel is a per-user-turn tally. It is reset on turn activation and summed from SDK result-message usage (input, output, cache read and cache write). So it reports what the SDK observed, not provider consumption, and an interrupted segment with no result usage would be missing. It also sits outside the stable ACP v1 PromptResponse, which at schema-v1.24.1 carries only stopReason and _meta.

Over claude-agent-sdk-python (proposed in round 1, so not re-proposed here) the adapter adds three things: a protocol-level session API (list, resume, load and close over stdio, usable from any ACP client), cancel-with-usage, and wedge recovery. The cost is a Node runtime and a translation hop. The comparison below decides whether it closes the Claude arm's 'usage unavailable'; provider consumption stays open either way.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn:

- Then run session/resume in a new process and check recall of a turn-1 value.
- Then supply a custom tool as a session mcpServers entry.
Keep the adapter as the Claude control lane only if its cancel usage matches the JSONL sums where the direct SDK reports none, and resume and the tool round trip match the direct SDK.

The typed @opencode-ai/sdk 1.18.34 client connects to a running server by baseUrl. Custom tools are typed tool() definitions from @opencode-ai/plugin. Auth is native ChatGPT Plus/Pro OAuth (docs: 'all the OpenAI models should be available') or any OpenAI-compatible baseURL (the OmniRoute lane, or LM Studio/vLLM on the RTX 4090). A macOS host could therefore drive a worker on the GPU workstation through a documented HTTP API. Not targeted, for three reasons. No application names a cross-host worker. The docs banner says 'OpenCode v2 is now available' while GitHub Latest is v1.18.34 and dev carries packages/sdk-next, so the SDK pin is about to churn. The server surface has three 2026 advisories: GHSA-vxw4-wv6m-9hhh (unauthenticated server command execution, fixed 1.0.216), GHSA-c83v-7274-4vgp (critical web-UI XSS, fixed 1.1.10) and GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4 (high, 2026-09-24, a cross-site server upgrade request can install packages, fixed 1.18.22). Arm A1 is codex app-server --listen unix:// over an SSH-forwarded socket through the Codex SDK protocol. Arm A2 (secondary) is --listen ws://127.0.0.1 with capability-token ws-auth. Accounting follows the 2026-10-03 design (usage, events, external effects, cancellation, recovery), with five measures: event fidelity against native logs, typed custom-tool round trip, abort with usage, resume after a server restart, and unauthenticated-access probes on every listener. Cases are scored as Harbor tasks. B wins only with equal task acceptance and complete receipts.

candidates.demonstrated_gap:
This is the closest maintained fit for overturn_when's 'durable multi-host state/replay' without running a Temporal server.

At v2.54.0, durable_exec ships dbos/, prefect/ and temporal/ packages, and the docs list eight engines. DBOS 'runs fully in-process as a library'. It checkpoints model requests and MCP calls into Postgres or SQLite and resumes workflows from the last completed step after a restart. A multi-host setup needs Postgres, because SQLite is single-host; the docs recommend Postgres for production.

Fit limits:
- It runs its own agent loop and reuses neither Codex's sandbox and approvals nor Claude Code's.
- Its openai_codex provider can keep the Codex subscription route: it calls https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex with credentials parsed from the Codex CLI's ~/.codex/auth.json. That shares the native OAuth refresh token with a second client, against the stack's 'native sign-ins left native' rule.
- The models/ and providers/ listings show no Claude Code subscription provider, so Claude needs an Anthropic API key or an OpenAI-compatible gateway through a custom base_url.
- Under DBOS, a CancellationToken cannot be passed to a durable run, and RunContext.cancel() raises UserError. This conflicts with the layer's cancel requirement.
- The docs note that durability is not storage, so it does not answer multi-turn resume; native thread/resume already covers that.

LangGraph checkpointers persist per-thread graph state for continuity, human-in-the-loop, time travel and fault tolerance, which is a different granularity from per-step durable execution.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The winners carry no SEP-414 trace context. A tool call bridged by mcporter therefore cannot join an OpenTelemetry trace. agentgateway v1.6.0 copies the W3C trace keys into every upstream MCP message's _meta (crates/agentgateway/src/mcp/upstream/mod.rs L115-118, applied at L347 and L404, unit test L887-900). In v1.6.0, CEL policies can match mcp.methodName such as tools/call, and RBAC evaluation populates it (#3197). The release also adds SSE keep-alive on long-lived MCP streams. Serving both modern (2026-07-28) and legacy clients (upstream/mod.rs L177, L465) is only parity: `mcporter serve` already bridges both eras (mcporter CHANGELOG L239). The trial is feasible on both hosts without a cluster: standalone agentgateway-linux-amd64 and agentgateway-darwin-arm64 binaries ship with .sha256 files. Maintenance is high, with 775 default-branch commits since 2026-07-08. Advisory status is unassessed: the GitHub Advisory Database has no package under RUST/agentgateway. candidates.demonstrated_gap: Reopen with new evidence. The gap: nothing checks the bridge or the installed servers per protocol revision under the breaking 2026-07-28 revision. MCP 2026-07-28 (spec release tag 2026-07-28) is stateless. The conformance README says revisions through 2025-11-25 use the stateful initialize handshake, while 2026-07-28 is stateless with per-request _meta. A scenario that belongs to both revisions must therefore run once per revision, and 'Passing it on one wire says nothing about the other' (README L121-L170 at c37eec888e1c). mcporter claims both generations, including `mcporter serve` answering 2026-07-28 and 2025-era clients through one endpoint (CHANGELOG 0.13.0 at v0.14.2). No file in this layer's gap-wave2 receipt directory mentions 2026-07-28. So no receipt checks the bridge against the 2026-07-28 requirement set or compares the two revisions. The receipts cover bridge calls, lifecycle stages, Inspector tools/list and project-file scope. Conformance supplies the protocol organization's own frozen per-revision requirement sets (`server --url ... --requirements 2025-11-25|2026-07-28`) with expected-failure baselines (README L76-L89, L121-L216). New since the 2026-09-29 refutation: npm 0.2.0-alpha.12 was published 2026-10-01T12:07:36Z under dist-tag alpha, with npm provenance attestations, and it ships package/requirements/2025-11-25.yaml and package/requirements/2026-07-28.yaml. The metric is the number of requirements that pass in A and fail in B, which are the failures the bridge adds, per revision, plus run-to-run reproducibility. Adopt it as this layer's revision-conformance check if it runs without credentials and the A-B delta reproduces. Any bridge-added failure becomes a mcporter defect to resolve upstream-first. It is refuted if the pinned alpha cannot run the requirement sets without credentials, if results do not reproduce from run to run, or if the Inspector CLI already reports the same per-revision pass/fail.
